did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens by noting that there had been no war between Aram and Israel for three years, until Ahab decided to act to reclaim Ramoth-gilead.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, agreed to join Ahab and expressed their alliance by saying, “I am as you are ... my horses are like your horses.”
Did you know? Ahab gathered about four hundred prophets, and they all advised him to go to war and be victorious. However, Jehoshaphat asked to hear from a prophet of the Lord as well.
Did you know? Ahab said that Micaiah son of Imlah was hated by him because, according to Ahab, Micaiah never prophesied anything good about him, only evil.
Did you know? Micaiah described a vision in which the Lord was sitting on His throne, with all the host of heaven standing around Him on His right and left.
Did you know? According to Micaiah’s vision, a lying spirit was sent to speak through Ahab’s prophets, so their unanimous prophecies did not reflect the king’s true fate.
Did you know? Ahab ordered Micaiah to be imprisoned and fed “only a little bread and water” until he returned safely from the war.
Did you know? Ahab disguised himself before going into battle, while Jehoshaphat wore the king’s robes. In this way, Ahab sought to avoid being identified as the main target.
Did you know? Ahab was struck by an arrow shot “at random”—that is, without the archer specifically aiming at him—but the arrow passed between the sections of his armor and wounded him fatally.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat tried to send ships to Ophir to bring back gold, but the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber, so they never made the journey.
